card.title: PixelGrasp
lines: A robot arm learns pick-and-place from a single camera.
Behaviour cloning in MuJoCo  |  2,000 scripted demos  |  45 min on a laptop GPU
+ 299 / 300 held-out scenes solved (95% CI 98.1-99.9%)

card.title: How it learns
lines: A scripted expert (which can read the cube position) does the task 2,000 times.
Every frame is saved: camera image + gripper pose + the move it made.
A ResNet-18 is trained to copy those moves: image in, action out.
Then it drives the robot itself, from pixels, on scenes it has never seen.
card.footer: No cube position is ever given to the policy. It has to see it.

card.title: Results (300 frozen eval seeds)
lines: + Camera policy, action chunking k=8:  99.7%   (299/300)
+ Camera policy, single-step k=1:  99.0%   (297/300)
Scripted expert with ground truth:  100%
Do nothing / random:  3.7%
- Camera shifted 3 / 6 / 10 degrees:  91% / 73% / 55%  (not trained for this)
card.footer: Every number is produced by eval.py; commands in VERIFY.md

card.title: What went wrong first
lines: Run 1  30%:  the red goal dot is 17 pixels, its height is unreadable from one camera
Run 2   1%:  action chunking averaged the ambiguity away
Run 3  19%:  reached the goal 98% of the time, then drifted off
Fix: give the policy the target as a command, record the hold phase.
The cube is still found from pixels alone.
card.footer: Failure taxonomy per episode: never reached / never grasped / dropped / misplaced
